mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the same month indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous month - 10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressure and input costs, compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) rises above 4% indicates a supply shock with cost-push inflation, which reduces real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decline in the federal funds rate below 2% within a single month signals an emergency easing response to a financial shock, which boosts liquidity and risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -1.0 percentage point in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero in these episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth above 0.5%) combined with a stable consumer price index (CPIAUCSL change within ±0.2%) over six consecutive months signals improving purchasing power without inflation, which supports consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% AND |CPIAUCSL monthly change| ≤ 0.2% for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above the median market return in these episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months during a period of otherwise stable inflation (CPIAUCSL monthly change within ±0.3%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions that depress corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.0% for two consecutive months AND |CPIAUCSL monthly change| ≤ 0.3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS growth above 2%) alongside a decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (implied from GDPC1 and PAYEMS) indicates households are saving more and spending less, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 2% AND implied consumption growth < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero in these episodes (t-test p > 0.10).
